summary: I tried Google Playground, Google's brand-new AI game maker, and built a playable game in about 5 minutes. Gemini, Nano Banana and Lyria generate the code, art and music from a single prompt.

transcript.text: What if I told you that Google just
built a place where you type a few
lines, wait about 5 minutes, and get a
real playable game? With its own art,
its own music, its own animations. No
code, no game engine, nothing to
install. Hi everyone, I'm Akana, and
this is Build Code Labs. Google Labs
opened a platform called Playground on
October 7th, and I got in on the very
first days. I made two games. I played
games other people made. One of them
genuinely scared me. And I'll tell you
what works, what breaks, and what to
know before you try it yourself. Let's
start with the basics. Google Playground
is an experimental game platform from
Google Labs. You describe a game in
plain text, and it builds something that
runs right in your browser, on a phone,
a tablet, or a laptop. Behind the
scenes, three Google models work
together. Gemini handles the game logic.
Nano Banana draws the characters and the
backgrounds. And Lyria, Google
DeepMind's music model, makes the
soundtrack and the sound effects. So,
one prompt turns into code, art, and
music all at once. Now, the part you
need to hear before you get excited.
It's not open to everyone yet. Right
